dedupe_keys.name: industry energy tool for us manufacturing

description: The Industry Energy Tool is a National Renewable Energy Laboratory calculator for US industrial energy and greenhouse-gas scenarios. It starts from estimated county and Census Region end-use energy for 2014, assembled mainly from facility emissions and the 2010 Manufacturing Energy Consumption Survey. Users set efficiency changes, equipment lifetimes and fuel-switching assumptions; outputs are projected fuel use and associated emissions by industry and area. Its scenario horizon can extend to 2050, while the base-year data remain estimates, not directly observed equipment stock. The GitHub repository documents the calculation modules and a separate, not yet integrated, hybrid supply-use model. Its licence is a custom permissive text with conditions on redistribution by research entities; the code is free to obtain, but the text should be reviewed before republishing modifications. The stock-turnover module uses shipment value as a proxy for capital stock and does not distinguish equipment vintages, which limits detailed plant forecasts. It serves industrial electrification and emissions planning. The catalogue's data-open-industrial-energy-asset-level-15min-manufacturing offers a different high-resolution demand source; no integration was tested. No data or code was downloaded.
